documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after pulmonology.

Pulm letter reviewed: COPD with FEV1 45% predicted, DLCO preserved. Started tiotropium daily plus albuterol rescue. Coverage sorted out in December.

He uses the Respimat every morning - demonstrated, technique decent, reminded to hold the breath. Albuterol a couple of times a week, mostly shoveling or stairs. Morning cough the same. No fevers this winter, no steroid or antibiotic courses. Smoking unchanged at a pack.

Vitals in flowsheet, SpO2 93% RA. Lungs: prolonged expiration, faint end-expiratory wheeze. Heart RRR. No edema.

1. COPD - added to problem list. Continue tiotropium + PRN albuterol. Up to date on flu, COVID, PCV20.
2. HTN - controlled. BMP today.
3. Tobacco - he asks what the patch costs; told him the plan covers it, he'll 'think on it.'

RTC 4-6 mo.

orders.reason: exertional calf pain, weak pedal pulses; vascular evaluation and ABI

documents.title: Office visit - leg pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Both calves cramp after about two blocks of walking, has to stop; a minute or two of rest and it eases, then he can go again. Couple of months. No pain at rest or at night, no foot sores, no numbness. No chest pain or palpitations with it.

Exam: Feet warm, cap refill ok. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses faint on both sides; femorals palpable. No ulcers, skin intact. No calf tenderness or swelling.

Impression: classic story for claudication in a smoker with HTN and lipids. Sending to cardiology (they do the vascular studies and ABIs). Already on aspirin and atorvastatin. Walk to the point of pain, rest, repeat - started him on that today. Smoking discussed in that light too.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation - vascular
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY CONSULT NOTE
Visit date: June 12, 2023
(Received by fax after records request 8/8/23.)

Reason: exertional calf discomfort.

History: 68-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, COPD and ongoing cigarette use. Reports cramping in both calves when walking more than about two blocks, relieved by stopping. Denies chest pain, palpitations, or breathlessness beyond his baseline.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, tiotropium inhaler, albuterol as needed.
Allergies: none known.

BP 142/88, HR 78.
Lower extremities: sparse hair over both shins, no edema, pedal pulses weak bilaterally. No ulceration.

Fasting lipids: total cholesterol 210, HDL 40, LDL 140, triglycerides 150.

Ankle-brachial index: 0.65 right, 0.70 left.

Assessment: Peripheral arterial disease, bilateral lower extremities.

Recommendations: Continue aspirin and statin. Structured walking program. Tobacco cessation strongly advised. Follow up here in one year with repeat ABI.

documents.title: Mail order
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Switching to the mail order pharmacy my supplement plan uses. Can you send all my prescriptions there.

documents.title: RE: Mail order
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Done - lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin and aspirin sent as 90-day supplies to the mail-order pharmacy. Your lung doctor's office will need to move the inhalers.

documents.title: Heart doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did the heart doctor send you anything from June? They said blockage in my legs and to keep walking.

documents.title: RE: Heart doctor
documents.author: MA
documents.body: We haven't received their note yet. I've sent a records request to the cardiology office today and will let you know when it comes in.

documents.title: Records request follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second request to outside cardiology for 6/12 consult. Spoke with their records clerk, will fax by early next week.

orders.reason: gradual central vision loss, trouble reading and recognizing faces

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV

Interval: Cardiology (June) letter finally in - PAD, ABI 0.65 R / 0.70 L, walking program. He walks most days, still stops at about two blocks. Breathing about the same on the inhaler.

New: Over the past several months reading has gotten harder - newsprint, his phone - and a couple of times he didn't recognize a neighbor until they spoke. Drugstore readers haven't helped. No eye pain, no red eye.

Functional: independent, drives short distances in daylight, no falls. Hearing ok. PHQ-2 0. Alcohol occasional. Still 1 ppd.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Lungs prolonged exhale, no crackles. Heart regular. Distal pulses faint. No foot lesions. Visual acuity by Snellen reduced both eyes with glasses.

Plan:
- Vision change: referred to ophthalmology.
- PAD: on ASA + atorvastatin; keep walking.
- COPD: continue tiotropium.
- HTN: CMP, CBC today.
- Vaccines: flu, updated COVID and RSV next month at nurse visit (COPD, age).
- Advance directive packet given, he'll look it over.

documents.title: Fall immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three shots today: high-dose flu and updated COVID in the L arm (separate sites), RSV in the R arm. Counseled he may feel tired tomorrow. Observed, no reaction. Eye appointment is set for late December.

documents.title: Ophthalmology consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY
Examination date: 12/27/2023
Copy to primary care (received 3/5/24 after request).

History: 68 y/o man referred for slowly worsening vision over months. Reading is harder and faces are hard to make out across a room. No pain, redness or discharge. Systemic history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, COPD, peripheral arterial disease; current smoker.

Visual acuity (best corrected): OD 20/60, OS 20/50.
Confrontation fields: full OU.
Pupils equal and reactive, no APD. IOP normal OU.
Anterior segment: quiet OU.
Dilated fundus: multiple drusen with pigmentary change in the macula of each eye. No hemorrhage, no subretinal or intraretinal fluid. Discs and vessels otherwise unremarkable.
Amsler grid: central distortion of lines in each eye.

Impression: Age-related macular degeneration, nonexudative (dry), both eyes, with reduced central acuity.

Plan: Daily home Amsler grid; call promptly for new distortion, a dark spot or sudden change. Smoking cessation advised - smoking accelerates macular degeneration. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Tiotropium renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual coverage renewal for tiotropium Respimat. Submitted with pulm letter and PFTs from 12/2022. Approved through 1/2025 same day.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Saw the eye specialist right after Christmas. Per pt: 'macular degeneration, the dry kind, both eyes.' Given an Amsler grid for the fridge; no shots, recheck in the summer. No letter here yet - requested.

Otherwise: calves the same, walks most days. Breathing steady, albuterol a few times a week. No hospital visits.

Vitals per flowsheet, BP fine. Lungs with prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. Feet warm, no lesions.

A/P
- AMD, dry, bilateral - per patient report, added to problem list. Amsler daily. Another reason to stop smoking; he heard that from the eye doctor too.
- COPD, PAD, HTN - stable, no changes.
RTC summer.

documents.title: Ophthalmology note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 12/27 ophthalmology consult received and reviewed. Dry AMD both eyes, BCVA 20/60 and 20/50. Matches what he told me. Monitoring only.

conditions.label: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of both legs with intermittent claudication

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 06/12/2024

69M, PAD, HTN, HLD, COPD, active smoker. Back for the leg symptoms. Still gets calf pain after roughly two blocks and has to stop; it limits him more than last year. Also notes erectile difficulty over recent months.

Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 40, ASA 81, tiotropium, albuterol PRN.
NKDA.

BP 142/88  HR 78
Legs: hair loss over both lower legs, pallor with elevation, slow capillary refill, diminished pulses in both feet. No wounds.

Fasting lipid panel: TC 220, HDL 35, LDL 160, TG 150.
ABI: 0.65 R, 0.70 L - unchanged from 2023.

IMPRESSION
1. Atherosclerosis of the native arteries of both legs with intermittent claudication. Stable ABIs.
2. Erectile dysfunction, likely vasculogenic.
3. Tobacco use.

PLAN
Continue aspirin and atorvastatin. Walking program. Cessation counseled. RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: cardiology letter from 6/12 in chart - ABIs unchanged, claudication bilateral, ED noted. Problem list cleaned up (PAD entry replaced with the claudication diagnosis).

He's still walking, 'two blocks, rest, two more.' Raised the ED himself, mostly wanted to know if it was 'the circulation thing' - yes, likely. Not interested in pursuing anything for it.

Breathing about the same. Still smoking a pack.

Vitals per flowsheet; BP fine here. Lungs prolonged expiration. Heart regular. Feet cool, faint pulses, skin intact.

Plan: same meds. BMP today. Talked through how smoking ties together the legs, lungs and eyes - he listened, not ready. Flu/COVID in Oct.

documents.body: High-dose flu R deltoid, 2024-25 COVID L deltoid. Tolerated. Reminded him the lung doctor follow-up is due - he has it in December.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY FOLLOW-UP (outside)
Seen 12/10/2024. Note faxed 1/14/2025.

Mr. Keane returns. Breathlessness has worsened over the past several months. Daily cough productive of white sputum. No chest pain, no fevers, no weight loss.

Medications unchanged: tiotropium 2.5 mcg two puffs daily, albuterol as needed, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin.
NKDA. Smoking 1 ppd, 40 pack-years.

SpO2 92% on room air. Chest barrel-shaped with increased AP diameter; breath sounds diminished, expiration prolonged with wheezes.

Spirometry: FEV1 1.0 L (40% pred), FVC 2.0 L (60% pred), ratio 50%.

Assessment: COPD with severe airflow obstruction, FEV1 lower than 2022. No exacerbations.

Plan: Continue tiotropium and albuterol. Again urged to quit. Return 12 months with spirometry.
